notes.text: The page continues a discussion of actions of pi on Lambda compatible with inner automorphisms of pi. It imposes a pseudo-partition condition: for each source object and each lambda in pi, there is a unique target for membership in the indexed subset, restated as a unique arrow of Lambda over lambda with that source. The left margin asks to examine separately this existence-and-uniqueness lifting condition for a morphism of groupoids. This is an account of the source; the condition has not been proved or inferred from a theorem.

The author says the condition gives the action on the object set and the way to reconstruct Lambda, with a displayed isomorphism and a functor to the one-object groupoid of pi. A t-like stroke below the object-set equation has uncertain attachment. The candidate preserves its visible position without asserting that it is an index or correcting it from the mathematics.

After two separate cancellations and an inserted On, the author supposes that the stabilizers are abelian, gives a family indexed by the quotient object set, and asks for the indicated action to be compatible with the functor. The extra closing parenthesis after pi in the family index is preserved. The E/Sigma and tau/T alphabets remain provisional, and the short word before the family may be grpes rather than fully written groupes.

The final author comment reads “Ce n'est pas bien élucidant” and continues “peut-être est-il plus agréable de”, ending unfinished on this page. The wording reports the author's own dissatisfaction and is not replaced with H's éclairant.

The margin reads ce condition without grammatical correction. The final compatibility clause has four continuation marks. The pencil numeral 24 at the bottom left is transcribed as a page numeral but assigned to an unnamed hand. H's description of the margin location is editorial and is excluded from source text.

Targeted verification of the reconstruction claim, conditional on the written unique-arrow lifting property: let p:Lambda→<pi> be the functor and let lambda·t be the target of the unique arrow with source t and label lambda. The identity arrow is the unique lift of 1, hence 1·t=t. The lift of lambda out of t followed by the lift of mu out of lambda·t is an arrow labelled mu lambda; uniqueness gives mu·(lambda·t)=(mu lambda)·t. Thus these targets define a left action. Sending an arrow to its source and label identifies its source and target, is bijective on arrows by the lifting property, and preserves composition by functoriality; it gives the displayed action-groupoid reconstruction. This check establishes that implication only. It neither supplies the separate abelian-stabilizer assumption nor determines the unidentified lower stroke or the glyph alphabets.

raw_difference_disposition: All 25 packet differences were inspected against the original and both native halves. Difference 1 is the editorial scan marker; 3 and 7 are gathered/array syntax; 5 and 14 arise from H's TeX thin-space macro after Ob, not source commas; 12 is H's editorial marginal-location note. These do not receive material rows. Differences 2, 8–11, 15–16, 18, 20–24 and 25 are covered by the abbreviation, margin, reconstruction words, deletion/insertion/suppose, family punctuation, plural, extension-glyph, final-comment and pencil-numeral rows. Differences 4, 6, 13, 17 and 19 concern the round-set glyph; the action-equation occurrence additionally requires M0708 placement review. Agreements were also checked, including all quantifiers, memberships, subset sign, primes, indices, brace, angle brackets, source wording, arrows, corrections and marginal writing. Additional issues found in agreements are the final membership punctuation, short group-word, extra closing parenthesis and fourth continuation mark; lowercase ce also differs from H. Certainty-only resolutions and macro-only differences are excluded from material reading changes. All nine crops were emitted and visually inspected; no OCR, web research or TeX compilation was used.
